name: object-segment-dynamic
instr:
Please support program-header-only ELF dynamic metadata in `/app`. Extend `object::read::elf::ElfFile::parse(data: R) -> object::read::Result<Self>` and `object::File::parse`. Don't add new crates.

When no `SHT_DYNSYM` exists, read symbols from the first `PT_DYNAMIC`, stopping at `DT_NULL`. No segment or no `DT_SYMTAB` means empty symbols. Otherwise require `DT_SYMENT` matching the class, `DT_STRTAB`, `DT_STRSZ` and a count hash. Use `DT_HASH`'s `nchain` when present, ignoring `DT_GNU_HASH`. GNU counts through the highest nonzero bucket's terminated chain, or uses `symoffset` for zero buckets; reject buckets below `symoffset`. Support ELF32/ELF64 and both byte orders.

Map virtual ranges within one file-backed `PT_LOAD` and the input using `p_offset`/`p_vaddr`, not `p_memsz`. Reject invalid metadata without panicking. Expose symbols through `elf_dynamic_symbol_table`, `Object::dynamic_symbols` and `dynamic_symbol_table`, with raw section/string-section/extended-index-section indices `0`; ordinary symbols stay separate.

`elf_dynamic_table` and `Object::import_libraries` independently use segment-backed bounded strings without `SHT_DYNAMIC`. Sections win for their respective tables, even empty ones; unrelated sections don't suppress fallback.

For segment-backed symbols, `Object::imports` and `exports` also use `DT_VERSYM`, `DT_VERDEF`/`DT_VERDEFNUM` and `DT_VERNEED`/`DT_VERNEEDNUM`. Pair address/count tags and bound list traversal by counts. Use existing filtering, order, na
